mot1921.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 (Ministry of Transport report on the collision on the Cambrian Railways)
mot1921.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921.quote: I have the honour to report for the information of the Minister of Transport, in accordance with the Order of the 27th January, the result of my Inquiry into the causes of the collision between two passenger trains, which took place on the 26th January, about 12.6 p.m., between Abermule and Newtown Stations, on the Cambrian Railways.
supports: date 26 January 1921
time about 12.6 p.m.
Abermule-Newtown single line
Cambrian Railways
report letter dated 8th April 1921, signed J. W. Pringle

mot1921casualties.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — casualty list
mot1921casualties.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921casualties.quote: The casualty list, therefore, totalled 17 cases of fatality and 36 of injury.
supports: 17 killed
36 injured

mot1921negligible.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — description of the tablet system
mot1921negligible.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921negligible.quote: This single line section has been worked by the electric tablet system since 1890, the type of instrument in present use being Tyers No. 6. The method is one of those which has been approved for single line working, and if the instruments are used fairly, and in accordance with instructions, the possibility of accident has been considered to be so remote as to be negligible.
supports: electric tablet working since 1890
Tyer's No. 6 instrument
accident considered negligible if used correctly

mot1921interlock.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — how the paired instruments interlock
mot1921interlock.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921interlock.quote: When one tablet has been taken out, the electric circuit controlling the two instruments for that section is broken down, and a second tablet cannot be withdrawn from either of the two instruments until the first tablet has been inserted in the relative instrument at the other end of the section, or has been returned to its original instrument.
supports: mutual exclusion is enforced electrically between the paired instruments
at most one tablet out per section

mot1921lettering.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — how tablets are distinguished
mot1921lettering.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921lettering.quote: The tablets also bear, in raised lettering round them, the names of the two crossing places to which they are applicable, i.e., Montgomery-Abermule, or Abermule-Newtown.
supports: the section name is cast in raised lettering around the tablet

mot1921numbers.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — the two recovered tablets
mot1921numbers.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921numbers.quote: There is full proof that the tablets recovered by fireman John Owen were those actually carried by the engines of the two trains ; the express train tablet being No. 18 for Newtown-Abermule section, and the down train tablet No. 18 for Montgomery-Abermule.
supports: both tablets were numbered 18
the down train carried the Montgomery-Abermule tablet

mot1921handover.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — the handover on the platform
mot1921handover.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921handover.quote: He handed the tablet holder, given him by Thompson, to the fireman without looking what tablet it contained.
supports: relief-stationmaster Frank Lewis passed the pouch to the fireman unexamined

mot1921examined.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — the express crew's check at Newtown
mot1921examined.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921examined.quote: The tablet for the Newtown-Abermule section was handed to Owen by foreman Brock. Owen examined the tablet, found it correct, and passed it to his driver for examination before hanging the holder on the hook. … he went to look for the tablet and crept under the frame of No. 7730 for the purpose. After a little search he found both tablet holders lying on the ground to the left (north) of the track alongside the wreckage of the two engines.
supports: fireman John Owen examined the express tablet and passed it to driver John Pritchard Jones to examine
Owen, injured, recovered both tablet holders from beside the wrecked engines
two passages from the same report, joined by an ellipsis

mot1921cause.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — conclusion and responsibility
mot1921cause.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921cause.quote: Indiscipline and slipshod methods of custody and transference of tablets, on the part of the traffic staff, combined with failure on the part of enginemen to examine tablets, could alone have made this disaster possible.
supports: the protocol did not fail; the handling and the missing examination did

mot1921recommend.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — recommendations
mot1921recommend.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921recommend.quote: electric interlocking should be provided between the single line tokens and the starting, or advance starting, signal giving access to the relative single line section
supports: the fix moved the check onto the signal that admits the train, and onto the enginemen

hansard1921.title: Railway Accident, Abermule — HC Deb 28 February 1921 vol 138 cc1396-7
hansard1921.author: Sir Eric Geddes, Minister of Transport
hansard1921.quote: four of the employés whose carelessness was responsible for the accident have been dismissed by the railway company
supports: four Cambrian Railways employees dismissed
the Minister told the Commons that if the regulations are obeyed 'immunity from accident is complete'
the question was raised as to feeling in Wales about single-line safety

mot1921release.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — the tablet released for the express
mot1921release.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921release.quote: At 11.56 a.m. the express was belled from Newtown. Rogers thereupon went into the tablet room, acknowledged the bell signal, and plunged on the Newtown-Abermule instrument to release a tablet for the express to proceed to Abermule. He did not inform either Lewis or Jones what he had done
supports: porter Rogers released the Newtown-Abermule tablet at 11.56 a.m. and told neither the signalman nor the relief-stationmaster

mot1921clerk.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — the fifteen-year-old clerk takes the tablet off the engine
mot1921clerk.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921clerk.quote: Thompson, who evidently was waiting on the up platform, jumped off into the six-foot way, and took the tablet holder from one of the enginemen. … Both Rogers and Thompson, lads of 17 and 15 years of age, were permitted, with the knowledge of stationmaster Parry, relief-stationmaster Lewis, and signalman Jones, to use the instruments
supports: booking clerk Thompson, aged 15, took the surrendered tablet holder from the down train's enginemen
two passages from the same report, joined by an ellipsis

mot1921assumed.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — Lewis's assumption in the booking hall
mot1921assumed.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921assumed.quote: As he entered the booking hall, he met Thompson, who handed him a tablet holder … and assumed that he had changed the tablet for the down train under the instructions of the signalman
supports: relief-stationmaster Frank Lewis assumed the tablet in the pouch had already been exchanged
two passages from the same report, joined by an ellipsis

mot1921nolook.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — the driver of the down train
mot1921nolook.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921nolook.quote: The driver of the down train was oiling his engine at the moment when the tablet holder was handed to his fireman by relief-stationmaster Lewis. It is clear that neither he nor the fireman could have examined the tablet before the train started from Abermule.
supports: neither engineman on the down train examined the tablet

mot1921conclusion.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — the two conclusions
mot1921conclusion.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921conclusion.quote: (a) that a correct tablet was issued at Newtown, with the co-operation of the traffic staff at the other end of the single line section, for the up express to travel to Abermule. (b) that the cause of the collision was the departure of the down train from Abermule with a wrong tablet in possession of the enginemen.
supports: the token grant itself was correct; the failure was at the point of use

mot1921rules.title: Accident Returns: Extract for Accident at Abermule on 26th January 1921 — the Regulations for Single Line Working, and the recommendation
mot1921rules.author: J. W. Pringle
mot1921rules.quote: Ultimate responsibility for leaving a tablet station with "the tablet for the section of the line over which he is about to run" is laid upon the engine-driver. … But this does not excuse the driver from the duty of examining the token, and assuring himself of its correctness, before it is placed on the hook provided for the purpose. … (a) that the signalman, or other person in charge of the tablet working for the time being, is the "sole person" authorised to take a tablet from, or place it in, the instrument … (a) at stations on single lines of railway, which are passing places for trains as well as electric tablet or staff posts, and where it is not feasible to locate the single line instruments in the signal-box, electric interlocking should be provided between the single line tokens and the starting, or advance starting, signal giving access to the relative single line section
supports: the standing regulation puts ultimate responsibility for carrying the right tablet on the engine-driver, who must examine it before it goes on the hook
only the signalman or the person in charge of the tablet working may take a tablet from or place it in the instrument
the recommendation interlocks the token with the signal admitting the train to the section
four passages from the same report, joined by ellipses

unverified: Any monetary figure for the accident — damages, compensation or the cost of clearing the site. No sum appears in the Ministry of Transport report or in the Hansard exchange, so no money figure is claimed in the prose.

That Lord Herbert Vane-Tempest, a Cambrian Railways director, was among the dead. Widely repeated and named in the allocation brief, but he is not named in the OCR text of the Ministry of Transport report as read, so he is left out of the prose.

That Abermule is the worst single-line collision in British railway history. Pringle calls the accident 'unique in the annals of British Railways' but states no ranking by casualties, so the superlative is not used.
The booking clerk Thompson's forename. The scanned report's OCR renders it as 'LIAM THOMPSON' (probably William); he is referred to in the prose only by role and age.

The rank and title 'Colonel Sir John Pringle' given in the allocation brief. The report letter is signed 'J. W. PRINGLE' and the Railways Archive record lists 'Major J. W. Pringle', so only the surname and initials are used.
Edward Tyer's personal involvement. Only the instrument type, 'Tyers No. 6', appears in the report; nothing about the inventor was confirmed, so he is not mentioned.
The Railways Archive catalogue's publication date of 1st January 1921 for the report, which contradicts the letter's own date of 8th April 1921. The letter's date is used; the catalogue date is not.
That the tablets were brass. Widely stated elsewhere, but the report does not say what they were made of, so no material is named in the prose.
